title: Stairstep Table Format

illustrates.quote: Wide Tables: Stairstep Table Format. Limit this format to tables with four or fewer columns. For larger tables use the Listed Table Format in Formats, §11.16. (See Sample 11-26: Stairstep Table Format on page 11-54 and Sample 11-27: Subdivision Headings on page 11-56.)

print.caption: Vietnam War
headers: Where were you during the Vietnam War?
How old were you during the war?
How did the war affect Americans?
rows: I signed up for the Marines and served in Cambodia.
I was 18 when I signed up.
There was a lot of protesting against the war. It made everyone think about why the U.S. was involved in a war so far away.
There are some I don't want to talk about. But I remember my buddies and good times playing cards and wishing we'd get home soon.
I don't remember too much about it. I do remember my grandmother being worried that her two sons would be drafted.
I remember the news on TV almost every evening had something about the war.
print.notes: A four-column interview/survey table where each column heading is itself a full question, and every cell is a free-text, multi-sentence answer -- exactly the kind of table the stairstep format (four or fewer columns, per rule 11.18.1) is meant for.
print.printFeatures: Bold centered title 'Vietnam War' in a larger font above a bordered box; bold header row (the four questions) with a ruled line beneath; ruled line between the two respondents' rows.
